newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Friday due to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange but profit-taking pushed the contracts off their intra-day highs, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 20,200 yuan ($2,434) per tonne, rising 130 yuan. It opened at 20,350 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 20,400 and a low of 20,160.
January rose 80 to 20,080, February 100 to 20,100, March 120 to 20,180, May 100 to 20,200 and June 600 to 20,320.
Combined volume rose to 97,290 tonnes from 66,270.
Copper opened higher and moved at high levels before profit-taking forced prices down late in the session.
Traders said many investors, encouraged by heavy overnight gains on the LME, rushed in to buy early in the session, but then more wary investors offset their long positions at high levels.
"LME gains and good-looking technical charts supported copper's rise today," one trader said.
"But some investors were unsure of whether the LME would continue its upward movement in the short term, which triggered profit-taking," he added.
Traders expect copper to move around the key 20,000-yuan level in the short term waiting for further news from the LME.
Aluminium ended up. January rose 50 to 13,900 yuan per tonne and February 100 to 14,150.
Combined volume rose to 360 tonnes from 60.
